I will still do it much like I did before, just trim where money is tight and keep enough fertilizer on so I do not lose yield. On my 24 mu, I will keep most land in the usual wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton, because that is what I know and what people around me do too. I will put 18 mu into wheat-maize and 6 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the main fertilizer under before sowing, and topdress once when the seedlings turn strong in spring. I have well water, so I will give wheat three irrigations if the year is normal. After wheat harvest, I will rush in maize on the same 18 mu, use hybrid seed, give enough base fertilizer plus one topdressing, and water about two times if rain does not come right. Cotton takes more watching, but on 6 mu I can still manage it. I will keep fertilizer a little on the safe side, spray several times for insects and disease, and water it three times. I do not like changing too much in one year. I start from what worked last year, look at what neighboring fields are doing, and keep my spending where the yield can still pay me back.
